## Design source

The settings design is by **Khôi (Vo Minh Khoi, @VoMinhKhoii)**:
[#7790](https://github.com/tutur3u/platform/pull/7790) introduces sections and scoped
contrast, [#7791](https://github.com/tutur3u/platform/pull/7791) applies account and
preference panels, [#7792](https://github.com/tutur3u/platform/pull/7792) covers
workspace and developer panels, [#7793](https://github.com/tutur3u/platform/pull/7793)
covers shared and Tasks settings, and
[#7794](https://github.com/tutur3u/platform/pull/7794) covers domain panels.

The design groups related decisions into cards in a centered column. Labels and
controls align across rows. Hierarchy comes from headings, spacing, and hairlines.
Color communicates state rather than decorating every setting.

## Component map

These contracts describe the proposed completed stack, including #7794's inline
row default. They are not exports guaranteed by an earlier stack layer.

| Need | Shared component or source | Composition rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Settings navigation and content frame | `SatelliteSettingsDialogShell`, `@tuturuuu/ui/custom/satellite-settings-dialog-shell` | Shell owns the page title, description, scrolling, and mobile navigation. Preserve search, keyboard navigation, and URL behavior. |
| Related settings | `SettingsSection`, `@tuturuuu/ui/custom/settings-section` | One titled section with one divided card. Do not nest cards. |
| Compact control or value | `SettingItemTab`, `@tuturuuu/ui/custom/settings-item-tab` | Inline by default in the completed stack. Narrow rows stack automatically. |
| Table, tile picker, list, or textarea | `SettingItemTab layout="stacked"` | Give the content the row width. |
| Free-form content | `SettingsSectionBlock`, same section module | Align custom content with row padding. |
| Save actions | `SettingsSectionFooter`, same section module | Keep actions in the relevant card. Preserve existing save semantics. |
| Empty, loading, or error message | `SettingsSectionMessage`, same section module | Include an actionable recovery when available. `tone="error"` supplies an alert role. |
| Validated field | `FormField`, `FormItem`, `FormLabel`, `FormControl`, `FormDescription`, `FormMessage` from `@tuturuuu/ui/form` | Keep the existing schema and field error association. A row title alone is not an input label. |
| Basic controls | `@tuturuuu/ui/input`, `/select`, `/switch`, `/button` | Reuse focus, disabled, and error behavior. Do not restyle individual controls. |
| Contrast | `.settings-surface` in `packages/ui/src/globals.css` | Apply at the settings shell. Do not copy its CSS values into apps. |

`controlWidth` is a shared scale: `xs` = `w-48`, `sm` = `w-56`, `md` = `w-64`,
`lg` = `w-72`, `xl` = `w-80`, and `2xl` = `w-96`, applied at the row's `@lg`
container breakpoint. The classes belong in the shared component so every app
emits them. Avoid app-local arbitrary widths for routine controls.

## Layout, spacing, and typography

The shell uses `max-w-3xl` with `space-y-8`. Mobile content has `px-4 py-6`;
desktop content has `md:px-10 md:py-10`. The desktop sidebar is `w-64` and appears
at `md`. Row padding is `px-4 py-4 md:px-5`. Section headers use `space-y-3` above
the card. Footer padding is `px-4 py-3 md:px-5`, with wrapping actions and `gap-2`.
Use the existing Tailwind spacing scale rather than pixel literals.

The page title is `text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight`. Section titles are
`text-base font-semibold tracking-tight`. Row titles are `text-sm font-medium`;
descriptions are `text-sm text-muted-foreground`. Preserve meaningful instructions,
validation, and recovery text. Remove duplicate page titles and redundant slogans.

Inline rows switch at `@lg` (512px of container width), independent of viewport
width. At narrow widths, labels precede controls. Long values need wrapping or a
bounded scroll region. Review translated labels, long identifiers, zoom, and the
last reachable action rather than relying on a desktop screenshot alone.

## Tokens and themes

Use `bg-background`, `bg-card`, `text-foreground`, `text-muted-foreground`,
`border-border`, `border-input`, and `bg-accent` for their semantic roles. Use
`destructive` for destructive actions and existing `dynamic-*` state colors only
for meaningful status. Pair color with text or an icon and an accessible name.
Avoid raw hex, RGB, HSL, OKLCH, arbitrary color utilities, and decorative hue classes
in application components. Token definitions remain in the shared stylesheet.

The proposed settings scope separates borders, inputs, cards, and accent surfaces
in dark mode. It also keeps disabled input values readable at full opacity while
disabled buttons remain visibly unavailable. Do not extend these overrides to the
global product theme without a separate visual review. Disabled is not read-only:
values that people must select or copy need an appropriate interaction model.

Light and dark screenshots are separate acceptance cases. A semantic token name
alone does not prove sufficient contrast, especially for focus indicators,
disabled values, validation messages, and selected navigation.

## Navigation, forms, and states

With expand-all enabled or search active, sidebar groups are non-collapsible and
redundant labels for single-item groups are hidden. Otherwise the group control
collapses its children.
Keep active state, keyboard access, focus restoration, and mobile back navigation.
Do not add a chevron to a control that cannot collapse.

Keep form submission boundaries, validation schemas, permission checks, dirty-state
logic, confirmation dialogs, and pending-state disabling when composing rows.
Connect each input to a visible label and its error. Keep failed values available
for correction. Do not turn an explicit-save form into autosave during styling.
Put destructive actions in a final section with a destructive button and preserve
the existing confirmation behavior.

| State | Visible behavior | Review evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Loading | Skeleton follows the final section and row geometry; controls cannot submit stale values. | No jump to an unrelated layout; loading status is accessible. |
| Empty | Explain what is absent inside the section; provide a useful next action when permitted. | Distinguish empty data from failed or unavailable data. |
| Error | Section message with alert semantics and retry when safe. | Retry preserves inputs and uses the existing request path. |
| Saving | Pending action and duplicate-submission prevention. | Success and failure feedback match the existing save model. |
| Read-only or denied | Readable values and an understandable permission state. | No misleading editable control or inaccessible copy affordance. |

## Explicit state machines

Steve Ruiz's tldraw prompt, "find all of the implicit state machines in my app",
is a useful review question. Model each UI surface's mutually exclusive states as
one discriminated union. Do not scatter `isLoading`, `isEmpty`, `hasError`, and
`isSuccess` booleans across a panel. Keep valid concurrent concerns in separate,
named machines rather than forcing unrelated processes into one status.

This illustrative type describes a settings editor. `Values` is the domain's
validated form type, not an unvalidated network response:

```ts
type SettingsState<Values> =
  | { kind: 'idle' }
  | { kind: 'loading' }
  | { kind: 'empty' }
  | { kind: 'error'; message: string; draft: Values | null }
  | { kind: 'success'; values: Values }
  | { kind: 'saving'; values: Values }
  | { kind: 'disabled'; values: Values; reason: string }
  | { kind: 'stale'; values: Values; reason: string };
```

Loading cannot also be empty or successful. Disabled and stale states carry the
values people need to read and an explanation. Saving keeps the submitted draft;
a failed save transitions to error with that draft. Use a reducer or equivalent
transition function to admit events only in valid states. Render with an exhaustive
`switch (state.kind)` and a `never` check so adding a state requires a designed view.
Do not claim this illustrative union enforces transitions by itself.

Design every reachable state, including stale data during refresh, pending saves,
permission changes, and recovery. If a state cannot occur for a surface, omit it
and document why in its review evidence. Test actual events and recovery paths;
a screenshot of a manually selected state does not prove that users can reach it.

Khôi's section messages, form errors, pending buttons, and empty lists provide
presentation references for these states. The captured settings diffs still contain
query and mutation booleans. They do not establish that every panel already uses
this discriminated-union architecture. Preserve their behavior during extraction;
apply the explicit-state requirement to new and substantially edited UI logic.

## UI review checklist

- [ ] Use the component map; justify any new primitive against existing first-party callers.
- [ ] Keep one page title and group related settings without nested cards.
- [ ] Use semantic colors and the spacing scale; review any token exception explicitly.
- [ ] Verify visible labels, errors, keyboard focus, search, and mobile navigation.
- [ ] Are all states designed and reachable, and impossible combinations unrepresentable?
- [ ] Use one discriminated state per mutually exclusive UI machine, with exhaustive rendering.
- [ ] Exercise idle, loading, empty, error, success, disabled, stale, saving, and permission states as applicable.
- [ ] Preserve schema, submission, permissions, URL state, and destructive confirmations.
- [ ] Capture 390px and 1440px viewports in light and dark, with no horizontal overflow.
- [ ] Check long translated content, copied values, focus contrast, and the final action.
- [ ] Record exact source, route, theme, viewport, fixture state, and screenshot path.
- [ ] Distinguish source checks, browser acceptance, CI, and production evidence.

## Reference screenshots and acceptance

Khôi's source screenshots are in
[the settings redesign directory](https://github.com/tutur3u/platform/tree/main/.github/screenshots/settings-redesign)
after #7790 lands. The PR contains appearance, security, profile, navigation,
workspace, members, and personality examples. Filenames such as `security-mobile`
do not establish an exact viewport or complete theme coverage.

Fresh captures must use the merged stack and a deterministic, non-sensitive fixture.
The required matrix is account/security, appearance/preferences, workspace/developer,
Tasks, and one domain panel, each at **390 and 1440 pixels**, in **light and dark**.
Capture default and representative loading, empty, and error states. Store the
source SHA and capture metadata beside approved references. Until those captures
are reviewed, this proposal has no complete screenshot acceptance receipt.

## Enforcement proposal

Start with advisory diagnostics for raw color and arbitrary spacing in changed UI
source. Shared token definitions and genuine user-authored color data need distinct
handling. Do not auto-rewrite data colors or CSS measurements into semantic tokens.
Warnings need file, line, rule, and a suggested existing token or scale.

Visual CI must use the shared dependency cache and affected-input selection.
Include shared UI, tokens, tested surface source, fixture, configuration, lockfile,
and browser version in the result identity. Cache browser binaries and dependencies;
reuse a passing result only for identical inputs in the same trusted context.
Never share privileged caches with untrusted pull requests or skip required security
checks. Baseline changes require reviewed screenshots, not an automatic acceptance
of every image difference. This proposal does not install lint or visual CI.
